name: Hermann Göring
role: Nazi leader: Prussian interior minister and prime minister, founder of the Gestapo, Luftwaffe commander, head of the Four Year Plan (1893-1946)
summary: Göring was a senior Nazi who combined German nationalism with a claim to socialism meaning national unity and service to the community. He held that Germany needed the leadership principle in place of parliamentary democracy and one-party rule, fought Marxism and Communism with police terror, and sought to remove Jews from German life. As head of the Four Year Plan he directed the economy toward rearmament and self-sufficiency, and he also promoted animal protection and forestry.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As Plenipotentiary of the Four Year Plan he directed agriculture, raw materials and consumption by state control and held authority over the private sector, rather than leaving allocation to markets.

unions-good.rationale: He testified that the trade unions were dissolved because their leaders were tied to opposing parties and did not fit the new state; the German Labor Front replaced them.

property-fundamental.rationale: He directed compulsory Aryanization and confiscation of Jewish property at low compensation, and confiscated party property of opponents, while saying private property of ordinary opponents was spared.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Under the Four Year Plan he held plenipotentiary control over the economy including private firms, bypassing the Economics Ministry, and ordered registration of Jewish property.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He created and personally controlled the Gestapo, which kept him informed hourly through a provincial network.

strong-leader.rationale: He held that the leadership principle was the only possibility for Germany and wrote that the people want to be led, not to govern themselves.

empower-police-military.rationale: He remade the Prussian police, ordering ruthless action and shooting, and built the Luftwaffe; he regretted only that he did not rearm more.

decide-locally.rationale: He praised the law that ended the German states' independence so that the Reich governs all provinces, and abolished the Prussian Diet.

rehabilitation.rationale: He called for ruthless extermination of subversive elements, set up concentration camps, and saw rescue only for the misled masses, not leaders.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He wrote that theatres, music, film and the press had been purged and cultural life had begun to bloom anew.

gradual-change.rationale: He called for tearing away what is old and rotten, purged the Prussian bureaucracy, abolished the Diet and aimed at total revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: At the 1938 meeting he said Polish Jews' legal position in Germany ought to cease, and in testimony blamed Jews who came from the East during the war.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He praised Hitler for checkmating the League of Nations and withdrawing Germany from Geneva.

free-trade.rationale: His economic record centred on autarky and import substitution under the Four Year Plan, not liberal trade.

nation-first.rationale: He backed withdrawal from the League and Disarmament Conference and told Gilbert that the only reality is self-interest among nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred: he held that how a sovereign state treats its people is its own business, and rejected humanitarian principle as a constraint on greatness.

open-borders.rationale: He treated national borders and the legal position of immigrants, such as Polish Jews, as ground to restrict, and nationalism as central.

revolution-justified.rationale: He testified that until 1923 the party meant to achieve its aim even revolutionarily, and wrote that National Socialism carries out revolution continuously.

central-planning.rationale: He ran the Four Year Plan, which allocated agriculture, raw materials and consumption by central direction, and defended it as security against blockade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: As Plenipotentiary of the Four Year Plan he steered raw materials, labour and capital toward rearmament and import-substituting industries.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He replaced unions with the German Labor Front and removed strikes and lockouts, which suggests state-organized bodies for labour and employers, but he described no wage-and-price bargaining.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wrote that the totalitarian state meant the NSDAP's victory and its continuation as the sole political organization, and he enforced the end of other parties.

democracy-best.rationale: He said democracy had brought Germany to the verge of ruin and told Gilbert that democracy would not work with the German people.

workers-councils.rationale: He condemned the Munich council republic and its hostage killings, and wrote Marxists wanted nothing to do with the Reich.

right-to-secede.rationale: He denounced Bavarian separatism and said the 1923 putsch saved the unity of the Reich.

natural-rulers.rationale: He wrote that God had sent Hitler to save Germany and that the people want to be led and governed, implying certain leaders are uniquely fitted to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: He took part in the 1923 putsch, commanded the SA, ordered arrests and shootings in 1933 and 1934, and said all aims were to be achieved by every means.

separate-church-state.rationale: He wanted clergy to stay out of politics, but his government also appointed a Reich Bishop and jailed political clergy; contested.

military-superiority.rationale: He built the Luftwaffe and said he rearmed Germany until it bristled and regretted not rearming more.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He held that Germany should be led by Germans, supported excluding Jews, and treated the nation as a community of blood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He condemned Marxist doctrine and credited National Socialism with ending class war; he put the nation's unity, not class conflict, at the centre.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He argued that strikes could not be reconciled with citizens' duties to the nation, and wrote that the only duty is Germany.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: As Reich Master of the Hunt and Forests he protected species and created reserves; this was framed as authentic nature, not only usefulness.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred: he condemned Marxist doctrine as pernicious and rejected the proletarian reading of society, though he never addressed this claim about profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He founded the Gestapo and the first concentration camps to crush Communists and called Communism a plague to be wiped out.

collective-farming.rationale: He celebrated the peasant standing secure on his own hereditary land, no longer a commodity, and opposed the Communist programme.

conscription.rationale: He defended reintroducing compulsory military service and helped build the Luftwaffe under it.

total-state.rationale: He wrote that Prussia put its principles into practice through a totalitarian state and that movement and state had become one in a common philosophy.

national-rebirth.rationale: He wrote that a purged and purified Germany arose and called the revolution a rebirth of the nation from a corrupt system.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He pushed the Anschluss and Czechoslovakia policy, and as Four Year Plan chief wanted Austria's resources, then led the Luftwaffe in the invasions of Poland and the Soviet Union.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He stressed unquestioning personal loyalty and oath to Hitler, wrote that the movement forgives everything but faithlessness to the Leader, and required police oaths to the Nazi state.

single-common-good.rationale: He wrote that other parties merely serve material interests while Nazi principles aim at the good of the whole people, and that cabinet debates do not express particular interests.

national-self-determination.rationale: He invoked a plebiscite for Austria and the Sudeten Germans' case, yet he helped destroy Czech and Polish statehood; contested.

class-collaboration.rationale: He wrote that Hitler ended the ruinous war between classes and parties, uniting workers and middle classes into one nation, and that nationalism and socialism require each other.

workers-nation.rationale: He said workers must be made Germans first, attacked Marxists for wanting nothing to do with the Reich or a people, and urged NSBO factory cells to win workers for the nation.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He announced the Nuremberg Laws as a clear separation of races and proposed at the 1938 meeting separate train compartments and exclusion from theatres, forests and parks for Jews.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He wrote that Weimar leaders and labour bosses served their own interests and the system was corrupt, and that parliamentary parties ignored the people.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: He stated that every police bullet was his, protected officers who shot, and later called trial of a sovereign state's leaders by a foreign court presumptuous.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He testified that the Nuremberg Laws aimed at separating races and defined penalties for relations between Germans and Jews.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He announced the Nuremberg Laws, directed the exclusion of Jews from economic and public life, and ordered preparation of the final solution.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He said even a leader-principle government must rest on the people's confidence, shown by plebiscites, but not through electing officials; contested.

population-transfer.rationale: He set up the Central Office for Jewish Emigration in 1939, spoke of evicting Jews from the economy and ending legal protection for Polish Jews, and wanted controlled emigration.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He accepted force as a political tool: the 1923 putsch, the ruthless 1933 police orders, and the stated readiness to reach aims by every means.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He told Gilbert that international power politics is a perpetual struggle of conflicting interests and that empires achieved greatness without regard for humanity.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He confiscated the property of the Communist and Social Democratic parties, declared hostile to the state, and had Communist officials arrested.

separated-powers.rationale: He abolished the Prussian Diet and replaced it with an advisory Council of State he appointed, making the Prime Minister alone responsible, and defended top-down authority.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He stated that strikes and lockouts were abolished because they conflicted with the right to work and with citizens' duties to the nation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He framed Jewish prominence as provoking defensive unrest and held that unity needed a German-led nation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After the Reichstag fire he ordered 4,000 Communist officials arrested, and the decree suspending basic rights followed; he also justified the 1934 purge as national emergency.

party-controls-media.rationale: He wrote that theatres, films, music and the press were freed from the Jewish spirit and purified of subversive influence, and he supervised the Prussian state theatres.

party-commands-army.rationale: He testified that he and Hitler rejected Roehm's demand for control of the army and wanted no political influence on the armed forces.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He wrote that followers resolved to follow Hitler blindly in iron discipline and that the movement never forgives disobedience.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He defended Germany's withdrawal from the League and said Germany's treatment of its own affairs was a sovereign matter.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He swore personal loyalty to Hitler as sole leader and testified to authority flowing from the Leader down, including command of the armed forces.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He demanded patriotic obedience in war and condemned Social Democrats who appealed abroad against Germany.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He wrote that film, theatre, music and the press were purified of subversive influence and ran the Prussian state theatres.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: from his leadership principle, where authority runs from the top down and the people only acknowledge the Leader, not remove officials.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He testified that he always considered Austria part of Germany and supported the Anschluss.

death-penalty.rationale: He ordered police to shoot and accepted responsibility for executions, including the 1934 purge, and promulgated the death penalty for capital flight.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: He announced the Nuremberg Laws, which tied Reich citizenship to German blood rather than birth on the territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He described socialism as service to the community, said the blood of a countryman outweighs material profit, and carried out expropriations; he did not state a doctrine of property.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He said clergy making political speeches could be proceeded against like anyone else and that Hitler set up a Reich Bishop, but he opposed attacks on the church; contested.

leader-cult.rationale: He wrote that National Socialists regard the Leader as simply infallible, like the Pope for Catholics, and described mass devotion to him with approval.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He backed the incorporation of Sudeten Germans and Austria, calling the Sudeten question necessary to solve and Austria a part of Germany.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He testified that the Four Year Plan aimed to secure Germany against crisis and blockade through domestic production and replacement of imported raw materials; colonies are not mentioned.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He commanded the SA in the 1923 putsch, but testified that Hitler afterward chose a legal political path; contested.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He supported the Reichstag Fire Decree, which suspended basic rights, and rejected the Weimar system's limits on the leadership.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He abolished the Prussian Diet and wrote that Hitler could not govern in a democratic parliamentary way; the Reichstag was reduced to acclamation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: In 1933 he decreed an end to unbearable animal torture in experiments and threatened concentration camps for those treating animals as inanimate property.

animal-use-humane.rationale: He hunted and kept the forest for hunting while banning vivisection and some cruelties; later experiments were allowed with anaesthesia.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He said the fight against the Versailles dictate was his decisive reason for joining the Nazis, and backed the revision of its terms.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: He was a leader of the regime and the Nazi movement, and rejected such a founding principle by record.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He fought Communism as the enemy but defended the Nazi totalitarian state and leadership principle, citing Russia as another case of it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He said a political structure suited to one country could fail in another and that democracy was wrong for Germany at its low point.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He testified that Hitler refused to let the armed forces be politically conducted or influenced, and agreed with that line against Roehm.

office-by-exam.rationale: He staffed police and civil service by removing officials and promoting loyal SA and SS men, and appointed party figures to the Council of State.

job-guarantee.rationale: He called the right to work the basis of the worker's freedom and boasted of work-creation programs, though not of a state employer of last resort.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He wrote that the Jew pulled the strings behind all of the movement's opponents and that Jewish organizations abroad ran an atrocity campaign against Germany.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He told Gilbert that how Germany treated its own people was its right as a sovereign state, strictly its own business.

defeat-communism.rationale: He wrote that Hitler took up a war to the death against Communism, and told Gilbert he was its most violent opponent, citing the arrests and camps he ordered.

religion-illusion.rationale: He treated religious belief as a real support for soldiers and had his own marriage and christenings done in church.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He described National Socialism as a new synthesis that threw both Marxism and the bourgeois parties into the abyss, with neither the proletarian nor the middle-class programme.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He confirmed to Jackson that no more opposition was permitted, that opposition parties and obstructive individuals were suppressed, and that the secret police and camps served this.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He wrote that liberalism erred in thinking people wanted to govern themselves and that the people want to be led.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He described National Socialism as a synthesis of bourgeois nationalism and Marxist socialism, each needed by the other.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He wrote that God sent Hitler to save Germany, yet also said government must rest on the people's confidence; ambiguous.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He built and led the Luftwaffe and urged rearmament.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He built the Gestapo outside normal legal controls, held opponents in protective custody in camps rather than prison, and backed the Reichstag Fire Decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: As Reichstag president he announced the Nuremberg Laws, which restricted citizenship rights to those of German blood.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He instructed police to draw and shoot when attacked and to protect state and people, and said every bullet fired was his.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He wrote of the 18 who fell at the Feldherrnhalle as sacrifices, and urged that those who gave everything be remembered always.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: He chaired the 12 November 1938 meeting that planned to remove Jews from German economic life, transferring their businesses to Aryans.

independent-unions.rationale: He defended dissolving the independent trade unions and replacing them with the party-run German Labor Front.

person-over-state.rationale: He wrote that he and his comrades ceased to be private individuals and belonged to the movement and the people.

racial-pride.rationale: He wrote of the bond of blood among Germans and a purified German people, and defended racial separation.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: As Luftwaffe chief he led the invasions of Poland, France and the Soviet Union; he denied planning aggressive war and claimed peace aims.

language-defines-nation.rationale: He supported the Anschluss and Sudeten incorporation on grounds of German ethnic unity across borders, describing Austria as part of Germany.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He wrote that an iron ring of hostile nations had always surrounded Germany, which others wished to weaken; no specific partition plan is claimed.

arms-reduction.rationale: He claimed Germany proposed universal disarmament and demanded equality, but rearmed far beyond defensive needs and wanted still more.

capital-controls.rationale: He admitted promulgating the December 1936 decree on foreign currency, with the death penalty for unauthorized foreign accounts and forfeiture of property.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He told Hitler every soldier must do his duty and go to his death bravely, and demanded obedience from police and airmen.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The unions that bargained wages were dissolved under his testified policy; he spoke of the Labor Front and a labor program, not of bargaining between unions and employers.

sacred-nation.rationale: He wrote of the sacred seed of the German will, the sacred peasant land and the sacrifice of the fallen for the people.

farm-price-support.rationale: He praised Nazi measures that placed the peasant's land beyond the reach of money-lenders and ran agricultural control under the Four Year Plan.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He rejected the Nuremberg tribunal's legitimacy, calling trial of a sovereign state's leaders by a foreign court presumptuous.

defend-planned-state.rationale: He fought the Soviet Union's system as a danger to Germany and Europe and wanted it destroyed, not defended.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He told Britain a plebiscite on the Saar model would settle Austria's fate, but the Anschluss proceeded by force and pressure; contested.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: He wrote that the peasant's hereditary land was sacred and inviolable and cultivated a romantic attachment to German forests.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He abolished the Prussian Diet and parties, saying Hitler alone stood with both feet among the people while party leaders ignored them.

notes: Answers rest on Göring's 1934 book, his Nuremberg testimony and cross-examination (some self-serving, given in defence), the 1938 meeting minutes and the record of his offices. At Nuremberg he denied planning aggressive war and knowledge of the extermination, and minimized his anti-Jewish role; those claims are contested by the documents, and where record and testimony differ the record is used. Holocaust denial is left null because he denied knowledge and called atrocity films fakes without a clear statement that it did not happen. Three answers are marked Inferred and kept low. He claimed to be less anti-Jewish than Goebbels or Himmler but led economic persecution and signed the July 1941 order to Heydrich; that order is not used as an answer to any statement here.
